text:
Ava (Finance): Hey team — quick heads up, we noticed ~$32k of provider promo credits that expired last month but our Dedicated reserved commit invoices still show full charge. Can we confirm whether those promos should have applied to the reserved capacity line?
Liam (CloudOps): oof, that's annoying. Do we have the provider billing IDs and invoice numbers? I can escalate.
Ava (Finance): Invoice 2026-09-INV-0142 and cloud billing account: 0123-REDWOOD-GPU. Promo code reference: PROMO-Q4-2025-RED.
Sophie (Billing): Adding some context — provider promos usually apply to usage, not to reserved contract line items. But sometimes the marketplace credits map weirdly. If Dedicated commitment was purchased via marketplace/subscription, credits might not auto-apply.
Marta (Dedicated Ops): We provisioned the Dedicated pool in us-west-2 for that commit; purchase was through the cloud marketplace (subscription ID 77-DED-2025). I can pull order details.
Liam (CloudOps): If credits didn't attach at invoice time, cloud support can do a retroactive application, but need proof of eligible usage. Can you run a usage export for the commit window and tag the GPU SKUs?
Ava (Finance): On it — attaching the exported CSV in a sec. We looked for SKUs prefixed with compute.gpu and gpu-dedicated but not 100% sure of matching rules.
Sophie (Billing): Also check whether the provider treated commit as "recurring subscription" which they typically exclude from promotional credits. If that's the case, we might ask for a goodwill credit, but odds are lower.
Ava (Finance): billing-bot, can you pull the invoice ledger and show which line items map to the vendor subscription vs usage?
billing-bot: Pulling invoice 2026-09-INV-0142...
billing-bot: Found 3 line items: 
• Dedicated subscription (marketplace) — $27,450 
• Overage usage (on-demand GPUs/egress) — $4,832 
• Network egress (cloud) — $1,223
Liam (CloudOps): Looks like the promo should have applied to overage first. If promo expired before commitment billing date, it wouldn't touch the subscription line. When did promo expire?
Ava (Finance): Promo expiry date in vendor portal: 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z. Our invoice billing period ends 2026-09-05, so some overlap.
Marta (Dedicated Ops): That overlap could mean the provider prorated credits across usage and subscription differently. We should open a support case asking for a breakdown and request retroactive allocation to the subscription portion if possible.
Sophie (Billing): I can draft the support request. Need screenshots showing promo terms and our marketplace order ID. Also we should request at minimum reallocation of credits up to the amount of overage ($4.8k) then escalate for subscription if they decline.
Liam (CloudOps): I'll prepare the usage report and tag all GPU SKUs. Ava, can you send the promo docs and the marketplace purchase confirmation?
Ava (Finance): Uploading docs now: promo_terms.pdf, marketplace_order_77.pdf, and the usage_export_202609.csv.
Marta (Dedicated Ops): Quick note — if provider refuses to reapply to subscription, we should consider short-term reserve rebalancing: move some workloads to on-demand or other regions where we have active credits while we negotiate. That could avoid hitting committed spend for the contested window.
Sophie (Billing): Good ops fallback. Also, flagging for finance ledger: do not mark the committed spend as final until support case resolves — we might be able to apply a refund/credit.
Ava (Finance): Case opened: PRJ-3421 with vendor support. Message: "Request retroactive application of promo PROMO-Q4-2025-RED to invoice 2026-09-INV-0142, provide mapping of promo to marketplace vs usage." Case number: VND-987654.
Liam (CloudOps): I'll follow up in 24 hours. If vendor stalls, we should route to our vendor manager for escalation.
Marta (Dedicated Ops): Also let's add a postmortem item: procurement checklist to verify promo applicability to marketplace subscriptions before committing.
Sophie (Billing): Agreed.
Ava (Finance): Thanks everyone. I'll circle back once vendor responds. :thumbsup:
